title: BAC/10/2017 of Shashi Kumar Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
BAC No. 10 of 2017
Hon'ble U.C.Dhyani, J.
 Mr. Shashank Upadhyaya, Advocate, present for
the applicant.
 Mr. V. K. Jemini, learned Deputy Advocate
General, present for the State.
 Mr. B. S. Bhandari, Advocate, present for the
respondent no.2.
 A first information report was lodged against the
respondent no.2 for the offences punishable under
Sections 420/120-B IPC. When the applicants failed
to secure bail from the Trial Court as well as from
the Sessions Court, he moved bail application before
this Court.
 A statement was given on behalf of accused-respondent no. 2 that he is ready to return Rs. 5 lacs,
which he has received as earnest money from the
complainant. The accused-respondent no. 2 was
granted conditional bail by this Court on 06.03.2017
(corrected on 06.06.2017) with liberty to the
complainant to move an application before this
Court for cancellation of his bail if the earnest
money is not returned to her (the complainant)
within a month.
 It will be worthwhile to quote the order dated
06.03.2017 as below:
 "Learned counsel for the applicant
submitted that the applicant is ready to return Rs.
5 lacs (five lacs), which she has received as
earnest money from the complainant. Applicant is
in jail since 28.12.2016 and she has no previous
criminal history.
 Learned counsel for the State opposed the
bail on the ground that if the applicant is granted
bail she will flee away from the justice. On this,
learned counsel for the applicant submitted that
the applicant is ready to furnish reliable sureties
if she is directed to be released on bail.
 Believing on such submissions of learned
counsel for the applicant, this Court thinks that
the applicant should be granted bail.
 Bail application is allowed. Let the
applicant be enlarged on bail on his executing a
personal bond and furnishing two reliable

sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of
the Magistrate concerned.
 If the earnest money is not returned by the
applicant to the complainant, the
complainant/State shall be at liberty to move an
application before this Court for cancellation of
the bail of the applicant, in accordance with
law."
 Later on, on being moved a correction
application, this Court passed the following order on
06.06.2017:
 "Correction application is allowed by
describing that the money be returned within a
month from today, failing which, the complainant
/State shall be at liberty to move an application
before this Court for cancellation of applicant's
bail, in accordance with law."
 Despite a lapse of nine months, the earnest
money has not been paid to the complainant and,
therefore, the complainant has made present bail
cancellation application.
 When the respondent no. 2 could not secure his
bail on merits, he sought a concession from the
complainant on a plea that he will return the earnest
money which has admittedly not been done as yet.
Since the very ground on the basis of which the bail
was granted to the respondent no. 2 has not been
honoured by him, therefore, in such a situation, the
complainant has every right to move for cancellation
of his bail and this Court also thinks it fit to cancel
'bargained' bail thus granted to the respondent no.2.
 Bail cancellation application is, therefore
allowed. Bail granted to the respondent no. 2 is
cancelled. Accordingly, it is directed that either the
respondent no. 2 to surrender himself before the
Court concerned within ten days from today or else,
a non-bailable warrant shall be issued against the
applicant by learned court below for securing his
presence.
 This will, however, not preclude accused-respondent no. 2 to move for fresh bail before the
Trial Court on merits, if he is so advised.
 (U.C.Dhyani, J.)
 27.12.2017
 Kaushal
